function.name: user_mandates
function.description: Fetches the mandates associated with a user based on the provided user name and the status of the mandates. This API is intended for use by partners to retrieve information about their clients' mandates. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

name.description: The full name of the partner's client for whom to fetch mandates.

status.description: The status of the mandates to be fetched. If omitted, mandates of all statuses will be retrieved.

function.name: partner_mandates
function.description: Fetches the mandates associated with a partner based on the specified status. If no status is provided, all mandates are retrieved. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

status.description: The status of the mandates to be fetched. If left empty, mandates with any status will be retrieved.

message.content:
A **mandate** is a formal authorization or instruction that gives a person or organization the right to act on behalf of another party. In the context of our system (and many financial or regulatory environments), a mandate typically refers to: | Aspect | Description | |--------|-------------| | **Legal/Contractual Basis** | It is usually documented in a contract, agreement, or regulatory filing. | | **Parties Involved** | • **Principal** – the entity granting the authority (e.g., a client, company, or government body).
• **Mandatary** – the entity or individual receiving the authority (e.g., a partner, service provider, or agent). | | **Scope of Authority** | Defines what actions the mandatary can perform: approving transactions, making decisions, submitting reports, etc. | | **Duration** | Mandates can be time‑bound (e.g., a 12‑month term) or until a specific event occurs. | | **Status** | Common statuses include:
• **Active** – currently in force.
• **Pending** – awaiting approval or activation.
• **Inactive** – expired, revoked, or otherwise no longer valid. | | **Use Cases** | • **Financial Services** – authorizing a bank to execute trades on behalf of a client.
• **Regulatory Compliance** – granting a partner access to submit filings.
• **Corporate Governance** – giving a board member the power to sign documents. | In our system, mandates are stored and managed so that partners can retrieve them via the `partner_mandates` function, and clients can retrieve their own mandates via the `user_mandates` function. These APIs let you filter by status (active, pending, inactive) and, for users, by the client’s full name.
